about: Curated open-licence typefaces for wordmarks, grouped by voice. Every family is on Google Fonts (text_to_path.py downloads it on first use). OFL = SIL Open Font License 1.1: free for commercial logos, no attribution needed; the artwork is yours. Reserved Font Names only matter if you redistribute a modified font file. Apache = Apache 2.0, same practical freedom. Always confirm the licence line text_to_path.py prints from the font's own name table.
pairing_rule: One typeface in a logo, two at most (wordmark + descriptor). Contrast structure (serif/sans, geometric/humanist), never two near-identical sans faces.

groups.name: Geometric sans
groups.voice: modern, product-like, neutral-to-friendly; the default for tech and consumer apps

fonts.note: Neutral UI sans; wide, open; needs tracking tightened (-10 to -30) at logo size. Safe but common.
Rounder, friendlier than Inter; good lowercase wordmarks.
Quirky terminals (a, g, y); strong character for developer and design brands.
Low contrast, geometric, slightly warm; variable optical sizes.
Wide, confident, contemporary; good for caps wordmarks.
Pure geometric (Futura-like); round o, pointed apexes; strong at heavy weights.
Squared geometric with tech feel; crypto/AI brands use it a lot (so beware of sameness).
Elegant geometric with thin options; fashion-adjacent tech.
Friendly, balanced; fine default for consumer products.
Neutral with soft details; works for Cyrillic brands.
Built for reading ease; wide; good for education and accessibility-minded brands.
Vercel's typeface; crisp, Swiss; developer tools (very recognisable as Vercel-adjacent).

groups.name: Grotesque / neo-grotesque
groups.voice: serious, editorial, engineered; infrastructure, finance, B2B

fonts.note: Grotesque with width axis (Archivo Narrow/Expanded via wdth); strong caps.
Engineered, slightly rationalist; pairs with IBM Plex Mono/Serif. Hebrew and Arabic companions exist.
US government neutral grotesque; trustworthy, civic.
Compact grotesque with width axis; design-studio flavour.
Newsy, sturdy; media and publishing.
Early-grotesque warmth; good at display weights.
Clean, slightly narrow; versatile.
Lively, idiosyncratic; creative studios, food, culture.

groups.name: Humanist sans
groups.voice: warm, human, approachable; health, education, services, NGOs

fonts.note: Rounded terminals; kids, wellness, friendly consumer. Nunito Sans is the un-rounded sibling.
Adobe's humanist workhorse; quiet, trustworthy.
Ubiquitous; includes Hebrew. Safe, little personality.
Mozilla's humanist; technical warmth; many weights.
Minimalist humanist; soft.
Designed for low vision; distinct letterforms (great for accessibility brands).
Rounded, chubby, playful; kids brands; includes Hebrew.

groups.name: Serif (display and text)
groups.voice: heritage, editorial, premium, cultural; also warmth for food and craft

fonts.note: High-contrast transitional; fashion, editorial. Overused in weddings.
Soft 'wonky' old-style with optical size axis (opsz) and SOFT/WONK axes; food, craft, friendly premium.
Elegant display Garamond; luxury, culture; thin at small sizes (use for wordmarks ≥ 24 px).
Bold Didone-ish display; confident single-weight.
Sturdy transitional; law, publishing, trust.
Calligraphic roots, moderate contrast; storytelling brands.
News-style with opsz axis; journalism, research.
Condensed, chic display serif; studios, fashion.
Robust transitional; pairs with Source Sans 3.
Faithful Garamond revival; classical authority.
Roman inscriptional capitals (Trajan-like); institutions, film, heritage. Caps only in spirit.
The classic Hebrew serif (Frank-Rühl); newspapers, culture, tradition.
Hebrew semi-serif with calligraphic flavour; literary.

groups.name: Slab
groups.voice: sturdy, mechanical, friendly-robust; tools, outdoors, kids, coffee

fonts.note: Neutral slab; many weights.
Mozilla's slab; compact, characterful; tech with warmth.
Geometric slab; bold display wordmarks.
Contemporary slab, readable; good lowercase.
Tall x-height, rectangular; developer tools.
Typewriter warmth; pairs with Plex Sans.
Quirky geometric mono; retro-futurist.
Ligatures for code; mono with humanist roots.
Crisp Swiss mono.
Wide, heavy, variable width; bold tech display.
Condensed all-caps; ubiquitous in sports/events (sameness risk).
Heavy condensed grotesque; impact without Impact.
Condensed gothic; posters, news.
Wide, soft display; web3/tech-culture flavour.
Art-school wide grotesque; culture, music.
Art-deco-ish display; retro consumer.
Grotesque display with weight range; bold caps.
Heavy Hebrew display; bold friendly headlines.
Hebrew display with strong horizontals; posters, food.
Condensed Hebrew/Latin display with retro Israeli signage feel.

groups.name: Script and calligraphic
groups.voice: handmade, personal, elegant or playful; use with great care (legibility, cliché)

fonts.note: Formal pointed-pen script (Copperplate family); weddings cliché; fine for a single initial.
Spencerian/Copperplate formal script; thin hairlines (large sizes only).
Lighter formal script; beauty, events.
Casual brush-ish script; friendly; overused.
Surf-style brush script; retro food/drink.
Energetic brush; sport and food.
Handwriting, not calligraphy; notes and education tone.
Monoline script, 1950s; lifestyle.
Casual connected script, French flavour.
Chancery-italic-based script; elegant, delicate.
Hand-drawn condensed caps; cafés and crafts; includes Hebrew.

groups.name: Historic broad-pen hands
groups.voice: heritage, craft brewing, games, academia, church, fantasy

fonts.note: Uncial (round broad-pen capitals); Celtic/medieval; can read as costume.
Textura blackletter; newspapers, metal, beer; illegible to many at small size.
Modern blackletter display; streetwear, music.
Gothic-cursive hybrid; games.
Roman capitals with flourishes; luxury, film.
17th-century printing types; antiquarian, publishing.

Hebrew Source Sans; humanist, friendly, clean.
Rounded corners, bold weights; consumer and kids; very common in Israeli startups.
Open, geometric Hebrew; tech.
Rounded geometric; soft consumer brands.
Neutral, complete; pair with Noto Sans.
Classic Israeli sans (Miriam); institutional.
Light, elegant Hebrew with Latin; fashion, culture.

Geometric, clean; apps.

Neutral gothic; pair with Noto Sans.
